# Leak Detection

Return to Underground Storage Tanks (UST) Main Page

## Monthly Release Detection for Tanks.

Tanks must have one form of monthly release detection listed below:

### Automatic Tank Gauging (ATG)

Probes in the tank are connected to a console containing electronics that monitor product levels. Precise product level readings are made in frequent intervals and a computer processes information and determines if preset conditions have been exceeded.

Information on Automatic Tank Gauging (ATG) is located on page 91 in the Standardized Inspection Manual

### Statistical Inventory Reconciliation (SIR)

This method requires the operator to stick tank every day that it is in operation and send a record to a SIR analyst who performs special statistical analysis with a computer.

Some SIR analysis can be performed in house if an approved method is used. 

Information on Statistical Inventory Reconciliation (SIR) is located on page 132 in the Standardized Inspection Manual

### Secondary Containment and Interstitial Monitoring 

Secondary containment consists of a double wall tank, double wall piping, under dispenser sump, or tank top sump.  

Interstitial Monitoring is a method of continuous leak detection which uses a monitoring device between the walls of a double-walled tank. 

Information on Secondary Containment and Interstitial Monitoring is located on page 150 in the Standardized Inspection Manual

### Manual Tank Gauging

Manual Tank Gauging maybe used on tanks 2000 gallons or less.  However, tanks between 1001-2000 gallons must also conduct tank tightness testing.

Tank Tightness Testing

Information on Manual Tank Gauging is located on page 81 in the Standardized Inspection Manual

## Leak Detection for Piping

There are two types of piping pressurized and suction.

### Pressurized Piping

Pressurized Piping uses a pump submerged in the product and
maintains a positive pressure on the product lines even when product is not
being dispensed.

## E85 Information

E85 must be used in State vehicles that accept this type of fuel. If an E85 facility is not readily available, check the vehicle's owner manual for instructions about switching blends. If another blend of fuel is added to the fuel tank, fill the minimum amount recommended by the manufacturer that will safely allow travel to the nearest E85 fuel station where the fuel tank may be completely filled.  Typically, the vehicle must also remain running for at least 10 minutes to allow enough time for the fuel to properly blend. Failure to follow the manufacturer's recommendations about fuel may result in vehicle damage and/or voided warranties. Do not use E85 if the vehicle does not have E85 capability. 

Q: Why does ethanol cost more than unleaded gasoline at some stations?

A: More and more states - especially those on the east and west coasts - are switching from MTBE to ethanol. This "pressure" on the supply is causing ethanol prices to climb, even though the supply is currently meeting the demand. Retailers without contracts in place are subject to these higher prices which are then passed onto the consumer. To find stations with lower prices, consumers are encouraged to shop around as it is likely that other stations in the community will be selling ethanol at a lower price.

We will continue to keep you informed of news relative to new fueling stations and discounted pricing.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Nevada International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) Requirements

To comply with the International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA), you must keep accurate mileage and fuel records for travel in Nevada. All records must be original and kept for 4 years.

Nevada-Specific Rules

No Double Waivers: Nevada never waives both odometer readings and travel routes. Single waivers of either requirement require pre-approval in writing prior to an audit notice (NRS 366.650).

Software Limits: GPS or mileage software printouts are not accepted as original source documents. Auditing using "Best Information Available" get zero refunds.

Out-of-State Records: If your books are kept outside Nevada, you are legally responsible for all travel and examination costs incurred by the Department during an audit (NRS 366.150).

## IFTA Record keeping Checklist

Image

Trip & Mileage Records

✓ Date of trip (start and end)

✓ Trip origin and destination

✓ Route of travel (Mandatory in NV unless a valid single waiver applies)

✓ Beginning & ending odometer reading (Mandatory in NV unless a valid single waiver applies)

✓ Total trip miles/kilometers

✓ Miles/kilometers by jurisdiction

✓ Unit number or VIN

✓ Vehicle fleet number

✓ Taxable and non-taxable fuel usage

✓ Distance recaps per vehicle per jurisdiction

IFTA reference: IFTA Procedures Manual P540

Image

Fuel Records

✓ Date of each fuel receipt

✓ Name & address of seller

✓ Number of gallons or liters received

✓ Fuel type & separate totals (Maintained and compiled in separate totals for each fuel type)

✓ Vehicle or equipment fuel was placed into

✓ Separate totals per fuel type

✓ Retail and bulk purchases accounted separately

IFTA reference: IFTA Procedures Manual P550

 Cayuga County Weights and Measures also participates in the New York State Petroleum Quality Program. # On-Board Diagnostics System

OBD II stands for On-Board Diagnostics (Generation 2).
It is a standardized computer system built into all 1996 and newer light-duty vehicles sold in the U.S. It continuously monitors your engine's performance and emissions control systems to ensure the vehicle is running efficiently.

Beyond just passing a test, a healthy OBD system ensures your vehicle isn't wasting fuel or contributing excess pollutants to the air.

## What OBD-II Does For You

Image

### Early Detection

Catches emission problems before they become major concerns.

Image

### Fuel Efficiency

Alerts you to conditions that waste fuel and shorten engine life.

Image

### Environmental

Helps reduce emissions and contributes to healthier air quality.

Image

### Fast Testing

Most OBD-II tests are completed in five minutes or less.

## How does OBD work

OBD (On-Board Diagnostics) is an internal computer that monitors your vehicle's engine and emission systems.

  * Detection: When sensors detect a malfunction, the computer stores a Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) and turns on the "Check Engine" light.
No appointment is needed, but arrive before 4:30 p.m.

Image

### If You Fail

You will receive a report detailing why the vehicle failed.

  * Repairs: You must have the vehicle repaired and pass a re-test to complete your registration. For emissions-related repairs, it is recommended to use a licensed 2G repair station.
  * Waivers: If your vehicle still fails after documented repairs at a 2G station, $450 minimum spent in Clark County or $200 in Washoe County, you may apply for an emissions waiver.
  * Permits: If your registration expires while you are making repairs, visit the DMV or go online to request a 10-day movement permit for $1 to keep you legal on the road.

## Do's and Don'ts

Image

DO: Act on Warning Lights

If your “Check Engine” or “Service Engine Soon” light stays lit, seek service immediately. Even if the car feels like it’s running normally, it is likely emitting higher pollution levels and wasting fuel.

Image

DO: Check Your Warranty

Some expensive emission components are covered by federal law for up to 8 years or 80,000 miles. 
Important: OBD catches “hidden” pollution by alerting you to fix emission problems the moment they start.

### [Button: How do I know there is a problem with my vehicle? ]

Your OBD II system is designed to alert you the moment your engine or emissions controls begin to fail. When a problem is detected, the computer stores a diagnostic code and illuminates a dashboard warning light.

Understanding the Warning Lights

The light will typically read "Check Engine" or "Service Engine Soon." Its behavior tells you the severity of the issue:

  * Steady Light: A problem has been detected that affects your emissions. Even if the car feels normal, it is likely wasting fuel and polluting. The vehicle will not pass an emissions test while this light is on.
  * Flashing Light: This indicates a severe malfunction that can cause immediate, expensive damage to your catalytic converter. You should take your vehicle to a repair technician immediately.

Image

Quick Fix: Check your gas cap first. A loose or broken cap is a common cause for the light. Tightening it may resolve the issue and turn the light off after a few days.

### [Button: How do I turn the engine light off? ]

The light will typically turn off in one of two ways:

  * Professional Repair: Once a technician fixes the issue, they will use a diagnostic tool to clear the code and turn off the light.
  * Automatic Reset: If the problem is resolved, such as tightening a loose gas cap, the OBD system may turn the light off automatically after a few days of normal driving.

Image

Warning: Do not manually clear codes or disconnect the battery to hide the light before a test. This erases the computer’s memory, causing your vehicle to be Rejected for being “Not Ready.” You would then need to drive the vehicle for up to one week to reset the system before it can pass.

### [Button: Is OBD going to cost me more money? ]

No. In fact, it is designed to save you money.

# Maintenance

Routine maintenance can prolong the life of your vehicle, help you avoid costly repairs down the line and keep you safer on the road.

Following are some important procedures and checks to follow:

## Read your Owner's Manual

Your owner's manual indicates the recommended frequency for oil changes and other maintenance services, as well as the specifications of vehicle parts and products you should use. If you no longer have the owner's manual, you can refer to the manufacturer's website for recommended maintenance. You can also look up recommended maintenance schedules on Edmunds' website. Keep a record and receipts of all your repairs and service so that you know when the next maintenance is due.

### Change the oil

Getting regular oil changes is probably the single most important thing you can do to keep your engine running well. Doing so will also improve your fuel economy. "Car Talk" hosts Tom and Ray Magliozzi recommend changing your oil and oil filter every 5,000 miles.

Color – The color of clear kerosene can be used as an indicator as to whether the fuel is contaminated or if it has been sitting in a storage tank for a long period of time and has potentially started to degrade.

Sulfur – Sulfur is a naturally occurring element that is commonly found in petroleum products. During the combustion process, this element can form sulfur oxides that are known pollutants in the environment (acid rain). Much of it is removed when processing crude oil into fuels and our testing makes sure it does not exceed those amounts.

Percent Fatty Acid Methyl Ester (FAME) or % Biodiesel – At the lab we use infrared light to measure the percentage of biodiesel in biodiesel blends to verify that the concentration advertised on the dispenser matches that of the product being sold.

Water and Sediment – Water is the largest concern for consumers when it comes to fuel quality as its presence can result in poor performance and possible engine failure. Sediment is a growing concern as more diesel engines shift to utilize high pressure fuel systems and, in some cases, can result in significant damage to fuel delivery systems. All samples are visually inspected for the presence of water and sediment during testing.

(2)  as a buyer furnishing the weight or measure of a motor fuel by which the amount of the motor fuel is determined, takes or attempts to take more than the quantity the person represents.

Sec. 2310.057.  USE OF INCORRECT MOTOR FUEL METERING DEVICE. (a) A person commits an offense if the person or the person's representative or agent knowingly uses an incorrect weighing or measuring device in:

(1)  buying or selling motor fuel;

(2)  computing a charge for services rendered on the basis of weight or measure; or

(3)  determining the weight or measure of motor fuel, if a charge is made for the determination.

(b)  For the purpose of this section, a weighing or measuring device is incorrect if it:

(1)  does not conform as closely as practicable to the official standards;

(2)  is not accurate;

(3)  is of a construction that is not reasonably permanent in adjustment or does not correctly repeat its indications;

(4)  facilitates the perpetration of fraud; or

(5)  does not conform to the specifications and tolerances under Section 2310.107.

Sec. 2310.058.  SALE OF MOTOR FUEL IN VIOLATION OF SUBCHAPTER. A person violates this chapter if the person or the person's representative or agent sells or keeps, offers, or exposes for sale motor fuel in violation of this subchapter.

Sec. 2310.059.  TESTING BY DEPARTMENT. (a) The department shall from time to time weigh or measure an amount of motor fuel that is kept or offered for sale, sold, or in the process of delivery, in order to determine:

(1)  if the motor fuel is of the amount or quantity represented; or

(2)  if the motor fuel is being offered for sale or sold in accordance with law.

(b)  If the department finds that any lot of motor fuel contains less of the motor fuel than the amount represented, the department may seize the motor fuel as evidence.

(c)  A person commits an offense if the person or the person's employee or agent refuses to exhibit motor fuel being sold or offered for sale at a given weight or quantity, or ordinarily sold in that manner, to the department for testing and proving as to quantity.
